(i) the problem of designing a cost-sharing mechanism that is incentive-compatible, budget-balanced, and economically efficient is NP-hard; and (ii) there is an efficient approximation algorithm that guarantees that, for every instance, the cost incurred is at most a constant times the optimal cost, the price paid by each participant is at most his true private value, and the price paid by every participant is at least his true private value.

(1) it is possible to quantify how much efficiency is being lost when one or two of the three goals are sacrificed in order to achieve the other(s); (2) the loss of efficiency is bounded, even when all three goals are not satisfied; (3) the loss of economic efficiency in a mechanism can be quantified in a way that depends only on the cost function, and is independent of the distribution of the private values; (4) this loss can be computed in polynomial time,

(1) it is impossible to design a cost-sharing mechanism with all three of these properties, and (2) there is a unique cost-sharing mechanism that is incentive-compatible, budget-balanced, and Pareto-optimal.
